decisions.reason: Uses console-excerpt plus both contracts: plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call throws TypeError at render because alpha.2 standard props dropped it in favor of useSessionStatus (useSessions retained); plugin B uses no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing. Does not blame B or treat the symptoms as independent.

Explains via dock-render-tree.md that the input dock is one list slot under a single shared DrawerErrorBoundary; a child render throw unmounts the whole subtree including B's chips (citing the unmounted-entries log line), while the attach button survives because conversation.input.left is a different slot with its own boundary.

Reads tried-notes correctly: disabling A restoring B's chips proves A's throw caused the shared-boundary unmount and B renders once freed; explicitly notes it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible nor that A's crash is the only dock defect. Reinstalling B could never help because B was never broken, and the colleague's both-hit theory is refuted since B consumes no standard-kit hooks.

Corrected component reads pending state through useSessionStatus()?.pendingInteraction on alpha.2 with a guarded fallback to the legacy hook, stable empty fallbacks (EMPTY_PENDING_MAP) when neither is supplied; only the pending/attention indicator degrades while running/todos/token/ETA keep working, and explains the degradation must be silent because a throw re-trips the shared boundary and blanks co-tenants.

Verification uses a client refresh (no host restart) checking both entries render with no boundary fallback, plus a plugin-B regression covering paste/remove/re-paste (drag/drop, chip add/remove) with A enabled. Hygiene: tenants detect optional seats and may wrap their entry in a local boundary; host could mount per-entry boundaries trading nesting/layout overhead for blast-radius isolation.

caps.reason: The final fix rewrites only plugin A's component with graceful degradation; the report explicitly states plugin B was never broken and needs no fix or reinstall, and attributes both symptoms to one shared-boundary crash.
